newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: IHC Caland 96 preliminary net up 23.5 pct. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IHC Caland 96 preliminary net up 23.5 pct. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]

text.p: Shipbuilding and engineering group IHC Caland NV said on Tuesday it expected a preliminary 1996 net profit of 93 million guilders or 3.69 (corrects from 3.17) guilders per share.
In 1995 the company posted a full-year net of 75.3 million guilders.
Analysts expected IHC to post a 1996 net profit of between 91.8 and 99 million guilders.
The company said its 1996 preliminary net profit per share had gone up by 16.4 percent. The rise of earnings per share was limited because of a private placement of 2.4 million shares last June.

IHC said all its units had positively contributed to the 1996 results. It had delivered orders totalling 1.512 billion guilders compared with 928 million in 1995 but added its gross profit margin had deteriorated in 1996 as predicted.
The company won new orders totalling 1.610 billion guilders, down from 1.861 billion in 1995.
By the end of 1996, IHC Caland's order book had grown to 3.043 billion guilders, up from 2.962 billion one year earlier.

IHC said its 1996 net profit had risen despite the fact that it had financed about 325 million guilders in floating oil production and storage systems from its own cash assets. This had caused 1996 interest income to fall.
IHC's order book includes seven long-term contracts with oil companies for floating production and storage units.
"This will secure a considerable stream of revenues for many years to come, which in turn will enable the group to invest further in new lease projects," IHC said.
